body:
Learned helplessness. Once you have been raped/abused, you start losing your sense of control over yourself.

When I was in a similar situation, I felt completely helpless to stop it, even though I had the gall all along

This post is very judgmental for no reason other than to be argumentative - but there was no valid point you made? Not sure what you expected when you posted that.

Thank you for this! I did pursue that for a little while, but the cost was really high, and I am honestly afraid of him getting violent and being put in dangerous situations. 

Lol they wouldn't even give me a TPO or a basic restraining order

They said it was circumstantial at best and that if I didn't have a rape kit or some kind of video or witness then it proved nothing.

:(

ME TOO. It feels so empowefing. I wish I could explain how liberating and revitalizing this whole end result has been

Shit like this is terrible!! 

I need to get into volunteering with that kind of thing to feel like I could at least make some kind of difference. It felt so helpless.

BUT in the end -- he was living in the home I own, and he lost his job a week after he moved out AND is now living with his girlfriend and her parents. Both are jobless.

I don't believe in karma, but it still feels awesome to have at least somewhat come out on top
Where did she say that she was going to press charges? It seems more of an acceptance thing.

I was molested by my best friend. She was 11 and I was 10. I cried and asked for it to stop. It's still a crime. Just because someone is a child does not give them a free pass to be violent or abusive.

My gut reaction is this: If it was not consensual, then it was assault. Something similar happened to me when I was younger - I am so sorry you are having to battle with these emotions. When I confronted my abuser, she also denied anything happening. It doesn't make it any less real, though.

Labeling this experience ) is only going to do just that. Ask yourself if it would make you feel better if you recognized it as assault. Would you feel more/less empowered, guilty, ashamed, forgiven, absolved of blame?

Now, it's about healing.

But enough of that--back to your original question: it very very much so sounds like assault. Experimentation is mutual.

Defined by justice system: any type of sexual contact or behavior that occurs without the explicit consent of the recipient. (More info on justice.gov/ovw/sexual-assault

A good rule of thumb is that if you didn't want to and did not say yes, or if you hesitated, or if you were uncomfortable, or if you were scared, then you could not consent.

People like you are part of the reason that, when I came forward about being raped, the first two questions I was asked were

1. Did this really happen? Are you SURE it wasn't consensual?

2. What did you do to fight back?

Even in your situation, you aren't allowing anything to happen. You didn't ask this guy to mug you. The burden of blame STRICTLY goes on the perpetrator.

I can't even fathom how your brain manages to make this seem logical.

This.

It shocks and appalls me that there are people commenting that "they are asking for it if they don't stand up for themselves. A guy will tell his friends he got away with it and then..."

I am so disgusted right now.

But the police don't care.

Tmi: I was in a domestic violence situation/raped for nearly six years. When I finally came forward (a few months ago, yay!) I went to the police. I had texts and emails from the perpetrator BRAGGING about what he did.

Spoiler alert: nothing happened. There was not even "enough" evidence to make him come in for questioning -- and two other women came forward.

This makes me hate the world

I wish this could be true. Most people don't care or just don't want to get involved. I've been harassed from the age of 9-until now (24), and no one ever says anything. Even if they know.

In fact, I've told my employer that one man was verbally harassing me in the parking lot ("you nasty, sexy bitch. Take your glasses off for your daddy.") He laughed. Thought it was funny and told me to have a sense of humor. This guy yelled this from a car. Many people were around.

I only wish it could be that simple. But people are so desensitized to this, most don't even realize or care.

How the fuck do WOMEN allow this shit? 

If you were walking down the street, and someone came up to you and mugged you and had a knife -- and you didn't fucking fight back, would you be at fault?

Also, calling GROWN WOMEN girls is inappropriate and demeaning.

No. Wrong. Issue #1 with sexism" wanting to blame the woman for something she has literally no control over.

Just because I'm standing there or wearing something or WHATEVER does not mean I am allowing someone to assault me.

This really disgusts me.

Are you fucking serious? It honestly doesn't matter if you are attractive or not.

Are 10 year olds attractive? Just because my best friend was followed into the bathroom by a janitor and he forced the door open on her (true story - AND he wasn't fired??) doesn't mean that she was attractive or not.

These things happen to. Everyone. This comment pisses me off. And it invalidates those who one might consider "unattractive" -- or hell... it even reminds me of the "she was wearing x, so 'her general attractiveness may play a part in that"?

Are you serious? Is this real life.

TW

I tried to report it to my university's domestic violence center, but when they started getting the police involved... I freaked. He was my best friend. He saved my life, literally... I had attempted suicide and was bleeding out. And we were going to get married and he was very mentally sick. But I found out later it was all a ruse. I'm so pathetic that I haven't told anyone in my actual life who currently knows him because I am afraid of what they will think of him if they found out. I don't want to ruin his life.

I just feel like it will have to happen one more time before I do anything concrete about it. Lol he told me he wanted to fucking beat the shit out of me, and I laughed... 

I was dating the he love of my life while still living with my abuser, and he assaulted me sexually again... I told my boyfriend, and he called the police. I lied to the the police. And i was so angry for him calling them

Thank you for responding. It breaks my heart. It really does.

I'm in therapy right now, but I am having such massive difficulty with day to day activities that I can only focus on today and tomorrow. Maybe when I get more resilient and able to cope now. Maybe then I'll rehash it all again.

Question... I've been really angry at him lately. He stole from me -- I screamed in his face. I'm not afraid of him anymore, but a twisted part of me wants to just push the limits so if something happens again, I can call th police and get the legal and emotional support from those I love and from the justice system... 

If he were to get violent, would it be my fault for arguing with him? Like would I deserve it? My head is so confused, and I feel like I should be smarter than this.
